sector: Food/cold chain (food supply chains in general; prototype with local stakeholders only planned, no case yet)
hitl_conditions: Human selects among Pareto-optimal solutions while training the ML engine; once confidence suffices the CDT decides autonomously, abstaining and escalating to the human when uncertain; abstention rate tunes decisional independence; active learning queries the user for labels.
key_finding: Design-science proposal (nothing implemented) of a Cognitive Digital Twin for food supply chains: DT domain (IIoT, VSM virtual model, LARG index, multi-objective optimisation) plus CDT domain (OWL ontology, knowledge graphs, ML engine) intended to decide autonomously, with selective classification (abstention) and active learning keeping humans co-piloting.
citation_locator: Key finding: Section 3.3 Defining a CDT architecture (pp. 7-8, Figure 3), Section 4.1 Defining a top-level ontology (pp. 8-9), Section 4.2 Outlining a machine-learning aided decision-making system (pp. 9-10), Section 5 Conclusions (pp. 10-11, prototype as future work). HITL evidence: Section 3.3 (p. 7, first VSM model via interviews and human auditors; p. 8, decision maker defines the VSM model, selects the optimal solution and trains the ML engine towards autonomous decision actions), Section 4.2 (p. 10, right to abstain, escalation to a human agent, human-machine co-piloting, abstention-rate trade-off = decisional independence, active learning as human-in-the-loop labelling), Section 3.1 RQ4 (p. 6) and Section 2.3 (p. 4, CDT autonomy 'without human assistance or limiting human intervention').

quotes.text: implementing a CDT architecture in food supply chains, able to handle multiple data-sources and conflicting goals under uncertainties, combining a DT framework, a lean, agile, resilient, and green (LARG) index and value stream mapping
The DT domain deals with establishing the connection between the IIoT devices and the multi-objective optimization engine, through a virtual model that relies on the VSM model and on the LARG index.
the decision maker interacts at DT domain level defining the VSM model and selecting the optimal solution among the ones delivered by the multi-objective optimization engine.

Doing so he provides a semantic description to the top-level ontology within the CDT domain and trains the machine learning engine towards a sufficient level of confidentiality to perform autonomously decision actions.

the models could get back to the user when they are not confident enough about their prediction. This should reduce the risk of inappropriate decisions from a CDT and allow human-machine co-piloting of a food supply chain.

quotes.text: Applying a Selective Classification implies an obvious trade-off between accuracy and the percentage of abstentions which, in the DSS4LCO initiative, translates into the amount of decisional independence of the CDT framework.
